question_text: Needle-like phylloclades are found in which plant?

The standard NCERT/textbook triad assigns needle-like phylloclades to Casuarina (Euphorbia's are cylindrical), so this card answers Casuarina and flags the conflict for teacher verification.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The plant
steps.why: The standard textbook triad is: Opuntia - flattened, Euphorbia - cylindrical, Casuarina - needle-like. The book answers 'Euphorbia' here, which matches the cylindrical form, not the needle-like one; this card follows the standard assignment (Casuarina).
common_mistakes: Writing Opuntia. Its phylloclade is flattened, not needle-like.
Writing Euphorbia (the book's answer). Euphorbia phylloclades are cylindrical; the needle-like form belongs to Casuarina.
steps.memory_tip: Casuarina looks like a pine - its green needles are the phylloclades.
steps.margin_note: One genus name is the mark. A teacher should confirm which answer the board key accepts - see the note.

steps.label: What a phylloclade is
lines: A phylloclade is a green stem of a xerophyte,
steps.why: Stating the definition and the three-shape triad shows why the answer is Casuarina and secures the mark even if only the plant name was asked.
common_mistakes: Calling the phylloclade a leaf. It is the stem; the leaves of these xerophytes are reduced to spines or scales.
steps.memory_tip: Flat pad - Opuntia; green pencil - Euphorbia; green needle - Casuarina.
steps.margin_note: The triad line answers every phylloclade variant of this question.
